newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Kohl says he does not plan cabinet reshuffle.
newsitem.headline: Kohl says he does not plan cabinet reshuffle.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl said on Thursday he was not planning a cabinet reshuffle.

Speculation had been mounting that Kohl's junior coalition partners, the centrist Free Democrats (FDP), might replace some of their ministers, perhaps later this year, to sharpen their profile in the run-up to the 1998 general election.

Kohl told German ARD television in an interview from his holiday resort in Austria that he wanted to continue to govern for now with the team he had. The interview was due to be broadcast on Thursday evening.
He said he did not plan to reshuffle any of his own Christian Democrat (CDU) ministers and said the FDP had not given him any indication that it wanted changes in any of its cabinet posts.
Kohl said there were no problems within the coalition, although there were always differences of opinion on specific matters.
Media speculation about a reshuffle had centred on FDP Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt being replaced, perhaps by FDP chairman Wolfgang Gerhardt, who does not have a cabinet post.

The CDU's Bavarian sister party, the Christian Social Union (CSU), is also believed to be lobbying for another cabinet post once the Postal Ministry, which it holds, is abolished by the end of this year.
